title: A standardized XRCT protocol for quantitative 3D shape preferred orientation analysis in rocks
content:
by Puqing Li, Vasileios Chatzaras, Matthew Foley, Sinan Özaydın, Patrice Rey

Quantifying three-dimensional (3D) mineral shape-preferred orientation (SPO) is important for interpreting deformation, magma flow, sediment transport, and anisotropic rock properties. X-ray computed tomography (XRCT) enables non-destructive measurement of mineral SPO in three dimensions, but few openly documented workflows link data acquisition, image processing, object extraction, and fabric quantification. This Lab Protocol presents an end-to-end XRCT workflow covering data acquisition, volume reconstruction, phase segmentation, grain-parameter extraction, fabric quantification, and projection of the calculated fabric onto the physical sample for oriented sectioning. An expert-calibrated machine-learning procedure returns reproducible, sample-specific loose and strict candidate minimum grain-volume thresholds (Vmin) for review before an operating threshold is adopted. Filtering at the adopted threshold suppresses the low-volume, poorly resolved object population and associated geometric aliasing, improving the robustness of the calculated 3D SPO. The workflow is demonstrated for spinel-bearing ultramafic rocks; application to other systems requires separate calibration and evaluation.
author: Puqing Li
